newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Chinese to build coal export yard for Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Chinese to build coal export yard for Nigeria.

text.p: China has been awarded a contract to build a coal export yard in Nigeria as part of the military government's drive to diversify from crude oil, a Chinese official said on Friday.
"A multi-million dollar contract was signed in December last year for construction of the yard," Zhang Zhongmin of the Chinese embassy in Lagos told Reuters.
He said state-run China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation would handle the job in the southeastern city of Port Harcourt, but did not give the precise value of the contract.
Nigeria's military government is trying to diversify exports, and become less reliant on the two million barrels of crude oil per day which account for over 90 percent of foreign earnings.
Zhang said Chinese engineers were due to arrive soon to start work on the project, which includes building a new coal loading quay with conveyor system.
Nigeria says it could export 15 million tonnes of coal a year from reserves estimated at 2.75 billion tonnes.
Shunned by the West for human rights abuses and lack of democracy, Africa's most populous nation has strengthened its ties with China and other Asian countries.
